requirements.statement: resolve each `/v1/messages` request's principal from the authenticated inbound identity, matching a `user` cap's `user_id` verbatim
attribute credential-injecting requests with no authenticated identity to a single anonymous principal that is subject to the organization cap

resolve, per period, a principal's effective cap as the principal's `user` cap if one exists, otherwise the `organization` cap, otherwise unlimited — the organization cap is a per-principal default, not a shared pool
check every period's effective cap before forwarding a request and refuse the request when period-to-date spend has reached any of them
refuse an over-cap request with a `429` Anthropic-shaped `billing_error` whose message names the period and its UTC reset time, appended with `blocked_message` when configured
name the cap that resets last when a principal is over several caps, and send `retry-after` with the seconds until that reset and `x-should-retry: false`

meter the cost of every upstream call made on a principal's behalf — the served response plus any routing-judge, classifier, advisor, or escalation call — from the upstream-reported token usage (input, output, cache read, cache write) and server-side web-search requests, priced through the pricing table, and add it to the principal's daily, weekly, and monthly counters
price a model the pricing table cannot place at a fallback unknown-model rate so no request is metered as free, and warn once per unknown model id
bill a stream that ends without the upstream's final usage report at a floor estimate derived from the output already delivered to the client
reset counters on UTC calendar boundaries — daily at 00:00 UTC, weekly on Monday 00:00 UTC, monthly on the 1st 00:00 UTC

persist counters under the existing spend state configuration (`state_path`, memory-only when empty) so a restart keeps period-to-date spend, and prune elapsed windows older than `spend_retention_months`

honor `[server.spend.enforcement] fail_closed_on_error` — when a principal's spend state cannot be consulted (its persisted counter record failed to restore, or the cap check hit an internal error), forward the request and warn by default, or refuse it with `429 billing_error` "spend limit unavailable" when set

add `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-*` headers describing the principal's own most-consumed cap to successful `/v1/messages` responses and to the spend refusal (`429 billing_error`) for a principal who has a cap, stripping every upstream `anthropic-ratelimit-*` header on every status of a metered request

serve `GET /v1/organizations/spend_limits/effective` returning, per principal and period, the resolved cap, period-to-date spend, and actor details, with `user_ids[]`, `period[]`, `sort=spend_desc`, `q`, `limit`, and `page` query parameters, authorized by read or write admin credentials
never block or meter `/v1/messages/count_tokens`
leave passthrough routes unmetered and unenforced, because those callers pay with their own upstream credential
document the enforcement behavior, pricing interaction, headers, and `/effective` in `docs/gateway-spend-limits.md`, the README locales, and the site reference

preserve streaming semantics — metering observes usage as a directly relayed stream passes and never buffers or alters bytes sent to the client; a gated capture, which the router retains before serving, is metered from its retained bytes
keep a metering or persistence failure from failing the response it meters
add no perceptible latency to requests, including for principals without caps
keep concurrent updates to one principal's counters lossless

resolve each Codex-endpoint request's principal exactly as `/v1/messages` does — the authenticated `[server.auth]` identity (static token name or verified JWT email), or the single anonymous principal when the endpoint runs without `[server.auth]`

check the principal's effective daily, weekly, and monthly caps before a Codex-endpoint turn reaches any upstream, over the HTTP routes and over the inbound Responses WebSocket, and refuse the turn when period-to-date spend has reached any of them

refuse an over-cap turn with HTTP `429` and an OpenAI Responses error envelope whose `type` and `code` are `usage_limit_reached`, whose `resets_at` is the Unix time the cap that resets last resets, whose message names that cap's period and UTC reset time (appended with `blocked_message` when configured), and which carries `retry-after` with the seconds until that reset

carry a configured `blocked_message` on the refusal in the `x-codex-promo-message` header as well, because the Codex CLI renders its own usage-limit text from `resets_at` and that header rather than from the error message
refuse an over-cap turn on an open inbound WebSocket by sending that turn a terminal error event carrying the same error as REQ-024, and keep the socket open for later turns
refuse the Codex CLI's web-search calls (`/alpha/search` and its aliases) for an over-cap principal with the same error as REQ-024, without metering them

meter each Codex-endpoint turn that completes from the upstream-reported Responses `usage` (input tokens, cached input tokens, output tokens), priced through the existing pricing table by the serving provider, the client-requested model, and the upstream model, into the same counters `/v1/messages` writes

price a Codex-endpoint model the pricing table cannot place — every GPT/Codex model unless the operator adds a `[[server.spend.pricing.overrides]]` row for it — at the existing unknown-model rate with the existing once-per-model warning, and add no built-in GPT/Codex prices

bill a turn that ends without the upstream's completion report — a dropped or closed WebSocket, a broken or cancelled stream — at a floor estimate made of the request's estimated input tokens plus the output text already delivered to the client
honor `[server.spend.enforcement] fail_closed_on_error` on this endpoint the same way `/v1/messages` does when a principal's spend state cannot be consulted
leave the endpoint unchanged — no cap check, no metering — when `[server.spend]` is not configured

document the Codex-endpoint enforcement, its refusal shape and what the Codex CLI shows for it, the WebSocket and web-search behavior, the floor-estimate rule, and the need for pricing overrides on GPT/Codex models in `docs/gateway-spend-limits.md`, `docs/m11-inbound-codex-endpoint.md`, the README locales, and the site reference pages with their `ko`/`ja`/`zh-cn` copies
preserve streaming semantics on the Codex endpoint — metering observes usage as the relayed stream or WebSocket frames pass and never buffers or alters the bytes sent to the client
keep a metering or persistence failure from failing the turn it meters
add no perceptible latency to Codex-endpoint turns, including for principals without caps

classify as an account-level refusal a response from an upstream the Anthropic adapter serves directly or through a Claude OAuth pool (a Kimi OAuth pool is out of scope and relays these unchanged) with HTTP 400 whose error message starts with `You have reached your specified API usage limits` or `You have reached your specified workspace API usage limits` (a spend limit the account owner set)

classify as an account-level refusal a response from an upstream the Anthropic adapter serves directly or through a Claude OAuth pool (a Kimi OAuth pool is out of scope and relays these unchanged) with HTTP 400 or 402 whose error message starts with `Your credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API` (prepaid or plan-included credit exhausted)

classify as an account-level refusal a response from an upstream the Anthropic adapter serves directly or through a Claude OAuth pool (a Kimi OAuth pool is out of scope and relays these unchanged) with HTTP 402 and error type `billing_error`

advance the failover chain to the next element on an account-level refusal, the same way it advances on a 429, both before response headers are committed to the client and inside an already committed streaming response
keep every other 400 and 402 response terminal: relay it to the client unchanged after the bounded body inspection, without trying another upstream

skip a credential the gateway owns (an API-key upstream, or one account of a Claude subscription pool) for new requests after it returns an account-level refusal, until the refusal's stated access-resume time for a spend-limit refusal, or for 1 hour for a refusal that states no time
rotate a Claude subscription pool to its next account on an account-level refusal before the chain moves to the next upstream, consistent with how the pool already handles account-scoped failures
never put a client-supplied credential (passthrough authentication) into the skip state, because the refusal belongs to that client's key and not to the upstream
hold the skip state in memory only; a restart clears it

when the chain is exhausted with no successful response and an account-level refusal was the best remembered failure, return it to the client with the upstream's own status and error message intact, under the existing preference order

update the failover contract and the user-facing failover and troubleshooting documentation, including every maintained translation, to describe the three refusals, the skip durations, and that all other 400s stay terminal
try a chain whose every element is in the skip window as configured instead of refusing locally, so a credential that was topped up or raised is noticed before its window ends

read an error body for refusal classification only for 400 and 402 responses, within a fixed budget, so other statuses decide failover from the status line alone (except where a path already buffers bodies for another reason, such as alias routes)
leave successful and non-refusal responses byte-for-byte unchanged, including streaming responses

log each account-level refusal at warning level with the upstream name and the refusal kind, log the skip expiry only for a credential that is actually skipped (not for passthrough), log the account cooldown for a Claude pool refusal, and count the advance in the existing failover metric
accept an optional [server.auth] jwt_header key naming a request header from which an inbound JWT is read, stripping a leading Bearer scheme when present
accept an optional [server.auth] jwt_cookie key naming a cookie from which an inbound JWT is read

verify a token found in a configured header or cookie against the configured [[server.auth.jwt]] entries with exactly the rules applied to a bearer JWT (issuer, audience, authorized party, token age, claim rules, identity claim)

read the configured header and cookie on the inbound Codex endpoint's routes only — Responses over HTTP and WebSocket on all three base paths, web search, and the client analytics sink — and nowhere else

try the credential slots in a fixed order — static token, then Authorization: Bearer JWT, then the configured header, then the configured cookie — and authenticate the caller with the first slot that succeeds
use the verified identity from a header or cookie token as the caller principal for usage attribution, spend limits, and account-pool session stickiness, exactly as a bearer JWT identity is used
remove the configured header and every cookie header from the request before it is forwarded to any upstream, on both HTTP and WebSocket

reject at startup a configuration that sets jwt_header or jwt_cookie without any [[server.auth.jwt]] entry, a jwt_header that is not a valid header name, equals (case-insensitively) authorization, x-api-key, cookie, a shunt-reserved header name, a header shunt itself reads or rewrites on the Codex endpoint (session-id, x-claude-code-session-id, content-type, content-length, content-encoding, transfer-encoding, host, origin, upgrade, connection, openai-beta, sec-websocket-*), or the [server.auth] or [server.admin] header name, and a jwt_cookie that is empty or not a valid cookie name

keep gateway-owned authentication failures on the Codex endpoint in the OpenAI Responses error shape and status codes — one undifferentiated 401 for a missing or rejected credential, 503 when no slot authenticates and at least one presented token names a configured issuer whose key set cannot be fetched
apply configuration reloads to jwt_header and jwt_cookie the same way reloads already apply to [server.auth]
consult the configured cookie only when the request carries no Origin header or one whose origin matches the request's Host
leave behavior unchanged for every deployment that sets neither jwt_header nor jwt_cookie — same accepted credentials, same headers forwarded, same responses
avoid disclosing which credential slot or which check failed in an authentication error or in logs at default verbosity, and never log a token value
